notes: Sepolia (11155111) test deployment, in constructor dependency order. MockOG is the existing 18-decimal test token: $owner receives its initial trillion-token supply and anyone may mint more. It has no economic scarcity and must never be used on mainnet. All application owners and the initial furniture royalty receiver are $owner. OGClubFurniture retains ERC-1155 supply, metadata freezing, two-step ownership and a 5% default royalty adjustable up to 10%. OGClubFarmVault holds unstake fees; only delayed Merkle allocations can pay tokens out. OGClubStaking uses that immutable vault, charges a rounded-up 1% unstake fee, and accrues 1e18 point units (one point) per whole token per day. OGClubRaffle uses those staking and furniture contracts and raffleNotice=0. Pools and prize lists are immutable after creation. This manifest makes nonpayable constructor deployments only: it cannot grant roles. Before creating the first raffle, $owner must make furniture.grantMinter(raffle) and staking.grantSpender(raffle), using confirmed deployed addresses, as the FIRST grant in each contract. Those two first grants activate immediately; grants made after any successful first grant require permissionless activation between proposal+7 days and proposal+14 days inclusive, with immediate revocation. Until these owner operations are confirmed, the raffle cannot spend points or mint prizes. The owner then sets the furniture base URI and creates raffles. Later farming seasons reserve at most half the unreserved vault balance, open after 3 days, and have a 90-day claim window; proposals are at least 7 days apart. Draws use an authenticated future block header and permit retargeting only after target+256 blocks; withholding all draws until expiry allows selection bias. Production uses a separate deployment with the existing OG token (no MockOG), a fresh deployer, OWNER a Safe, and RAFFLE_NOTICE=604800. See README.md for setup, permissions, token assumptions and randomness limitations. No deployment or broadcast was performed by this adaptation.
